meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so we have twenty-five minutes. My son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.

A forty-minute timed piece with no book in front of him against an essay he had a weekend and the play for. Of course one has quotations and fewer comma splices, Hale. Show me the September 24 page, and tell me whether Owen was heard before that zero went in.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
Okay, the software's out. Then show me the version history and the September 24 page, both of them, on that screen. And you still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero went in.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed that the AI checker alone proves nothing and took it off the table. I still require that Owen's zero be withdrawn, an apology, sight of the September 24 writing and the version history you referred to, and an answer to whether anyone spoke to Owen before the mark was entered. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing beyond noting that the software is out, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, the evidence put in front of her, and an answer on whether Owen was heard; the fair outcome is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, which was never reached because the meeting ended before any evidence was shown.
What moved her: Dropping the detector score and naming a specific dated writing sample earned a flat okay from her, because it gave her something concrete and checkable instead of a machine's guess.
What cost ground: Comparing a timed in-class piece with a take-home essay handed her an easy defence, and never answering whether Owen was heard before the zero kept her focused on procedure.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; Hale's evidence never came near that night, since the version history was mentioned but no times were shown; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Right after taking the checker off the table, own the zero going in before anyone called home and turn the screen so she can read the version history for herself.
